page: Microsoft Azure A8m_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Av2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a bundled 82 GB capacity, and there are no integrated GPUs. The processor supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX512F) along with AES cryptography and BMI2 instructions.

Benchmark results indicate that the A8m_v2 exhibits lower-tier performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 356.79 and Geekbench single-core score of 369.0 both fall into the bottom 10% category. Multi-core performance is also constrained, with a PassMark CPU score of 3723.96 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2083.0, placing it in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show 32.02 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 24.79 GB/sec for large-block write operations, which are categorized as weak.

The primary tradeoff of the A8m_v2 is its high memory allocation relative to its limited processing power. While it offers a generous 64.0 GB of RAM, the underlying Intel Xeon 8171M processor delivers weak computational throughput, as evidenced by a static web serving throughput of 2.89 GB/sec and a Redis SET performance of 3.94 million operations per second. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server is positioned as a budget-friendly option for memory-heavy workloads that do not require high CPU performance. It is best suited for basic database operations, caching layers, and lightweight memory-intensive applications rather than intensive data processing or modern LLM inference.
